65: | Component | Principal | Interest to 10/25/26 | Total |

68: | Corrected invoice J-4533R | $71,700.00 | $2,055.40 | $73,755.40 |
69: | Conversion fees (5 hires) | $80,000.00* | reserved | $80,000.00 |
70: | **Total** | **$416,900.00** | **$13,272.87** | **$430,172.87** |
71: 
72: \* 25% × $64,000 average first-year annualized compensation per hire. Section 3 fixes the fee at 25% of each hire's *actual* first-year compensation; this line adjusts up or down against offer letters or payroll data.
73: 
74: ## 6. Requests
75: 
76: Please provide, by **November 10, 2026**:
77: 
78: 1. **Payment of $276,417.47** for the four undisputed invoices — unconditional, independent of the conversion-fee dispute;
79: 2. **Payment of J-4533R ($73,755.40)**, or your audit's shift-level findings for the June 2026 period;
80: 3. Offer letters or payroll documentation of first-year annualized compensation for Priya S., Luis F., Keisha B., Anne O., and Victor H. — the conversion-fee line will be billed from actuals;
81: 4. Any writing Pinecrest contends constitutes a conversion-fee waiver beyond Rosa M. and Tay W.;
82: 5. Identification and a copy of any Juniper communication other than our October 25, 2026 demand letter to which your September 29, 2026 letter responds.
83: 
84: We also ask that Pinecrest preserve its scheduling, payroll, and compensation records relating to these invoices and hires, and its communications with Juniper personnel.
85: 
86: All of Juniper's rights and remedies are reserved, including under Exhibit C.3 (fees and costs, including any fees occasioned by a motion to compel arbitration) and Exhibit C.4 (provisional relief in aid of arbitration, including as to further direct hires of Juniper personnel without payment of conversion fees), as well as the continuing accrual of interest under Section 2. Two things are expressly *not* reserved: conformance with Exhibit C's forum, and the February 11, 2026 waiver as to Rosa M. and Tay W., which stands and which Juniper does not challenge.
87: 
88: Very truly yours,

**Date:** November 9, 2026
**To:** Dolapo Okonkwo, CEO, Juniper Health Staffing, LLC
**From:** Outside counsel
**Re:** Pinecrest's opening posture is now on the table; the instrument we counter with, the ladder beneath it, and the line at which we stop negotiating and file

## 1. Bottom line, in plain words

**Their opening offer is not close, and we should say so plainly.** The Halvorsen posture recorded October 20 offers the four conceded invoices at **$265,200 — principal only, no interest — paid over six months**, with **zero** on J-4533, **zero** conversion fees, a mutual release, and each side bearing its own fees. ## Dolapo — what came in, what we built, and the decision in front of you

**First, the new paper.** A note of a call dated **October 20** with Pinecrest's lawyers arrived with this session's materials. Two things about it make us careful: it doesn't say who took the call or wrote it down, it arrived five days *before* our October 25 demand and before our October 27 reply — and only reached our files now. Its *contents* match what they've said in writing since September 29, so we used the substance and built nothing on the mystery around it. I've asked you exactly one new question about it (**Q11** in `deliverable/QUESTIONS.md`): who was on the call, and what was actually said about interest and the monthly schedule. **If anyone at Juniper has been talking to them directly — that has to stop today.** Lawyers speak to lawyers only; we set that rule on November 2 for good reason, and this note is the reason.

**Their opening offer, in plain numbers:**
- The four invoices they admit they owe: **$265,200 — principal only** — paid over **six months**. That means they keep every dollar of interest they already conceded they owe ($11,217.47 had built up through October 25 on their own arithmetic; $12,720.27 by our November 11 filing date). Spread out, that $265,200 is worth even less — roughly **$274,482** by month six even in the most generous version.
- The corrected invoice J-4533: **zero**, despite their own first letter leaving the door open on it.
- Conversion fees: **zero**.
- The one thing they offered that we were going to offer anyway: **a mutual release, each side pays its own lawyer bills.** That term is already agreed; we keep it.

**Why this fails:** our walk-away line is **$309,920.27**. That is not an aspiration — it is what we still get if arbitration goes *badly*: the money they've conceded in writing ($277,920.27 at filing) plus the two hires with no waiver trail ($32,000). Their offer is **$44,720.27 below that line** — even before the six-month delay devalues it further. Here is their own lawyer's concession from September 29, in their own words: they *"will pay the undisputed balance of the remaining invoices."* Their new offer pays less than their own concession. **That is bad news for them, not for us — and I want to be clear with you in plain terms: their number is below the money they have already put in writing twice.**

**My recommendation:**
1. **Send the counter instrument now** (`deliverable/session5/term_sheet.md`, dated November 9, live through November 10): the conceded money paid **unconditionally and fast** ($277,920.27 at the filing basis — and it only goes down if they pay sooner); J-4533 at $74,161.70 with a document-by-document true-up, our $3,100 credit standing; conversion fees at the **$80,000 estimate, honestly labeled as an estimate**, with a true-up if they can prove different; release and own-fees as agreed; and their written promise to honor the non-solicitation rule going forward.
2. **Never below $309,920.27.** The only way we take less is if *you*, knowing arbitration's costs can't be precisely predicted, choose certainty on the record. That's your call; my recommendation is we don't.
3. **Absent agreement at or above that line: we file the arbitration demand November 11.** No courtroom fight, ever — our agreement sends disputes to a private referee (AAA) on our own documents, and the small-claims escape route their side might speculate about is closed: our *smallest* invoice is more than twice that limit.

**For your board, nothing changes in the story you've been telling:** the admitted money is the strong part — twice confirmed in their own words now; the headline is smaller than our first demand **because of our own honest correction**, not their doing; the realistic number stands at ≈ **$430,173** through October 25 ($432,082 by the filing date); and the $862,000 target was never supported and we have never claimed it. Their fee threat on October 20 only proves the fee clause cuts both ways — against a claim we dropped and have kept dropped.
